items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "dioyl dichloride"?

Polymerisation in which monomers join with the elimination of a small molecule such as water or hydrogen chloride.
A compound with two –COCl groups, used instead of a dicarboxylic acid to make polyesters and polyamides faster, with HCl eliminated.

items.answer: The C=C bond becomes a single bond in the polymer; the repeat unit is –CH₂–CH₂–.

items.stem: Kenji writes in a revision note: "Any molecule with two functional groups forms an addition polymer." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Molecules with two reactive groups (e.g. –OH and –COOH) form condensation polymers; addition polymers need C=C.

items.stem: A section of a polymer chain is –OCH(CH₃)CO–OCH(CH₃)CO–OCH(CH₃)CO–. What type of polymer is it?
items.answer: Polyester (condensation)
items.markingKey: Contains ester links.

items.stem: What is the repeat unit of the addition polymer formed from ethene, CH₂=CH₂?
items.answer: –CH₂–CH₂–

items.stem: A section of a polymer chain is –O(CH₂)₃O–CO–C₆H₄–CO–O(CH₂)₃O–CO–C₆H₄–CO–. Identify the type of linkage and deduce the structure(s) of the monomer(s).
items.answer: ester linkage (polyester); monomer(s): propane-1,3-diol, HO(CH₂)₃OH, and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid, HOOC–C₆H₄–COOH

items.stem: Priya is given samples of two polymers, X and Y. X has the repeat unit –CH₂–CCl₂–. Y has the repeat unit –OCH₂CH₂O–CO(CH₂)₄CO–. (a) State, with a reason, which polymer was made by addition polymerisation. (b) Give the structural formula of the monomer of X. (c) Suggest, with a reason, which polymer is more likely to biodegrade.
items.answer: (a) X: its backbone contains only carbon atoms (formed from C=C monomers), with no ester or amide links. (b) CH₂=CCl₂ (c) Y: the polar ester links can be hydrolysed (by enzymes, acid or alkali); X has non-polar C–C and C–H bonds only.

items.stem: State one advantage and one disadvantage of using biodegradable polymers.
items.answer: Advantage: break down in the environment, reducing persistent waste / often from renewable sources. Disadvantage: may need specific composting conditions; can be weaker / more expensive; may contaminate recycling.
items.markingKey: advantage [1]; disadvantage [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why PLA is described as both renewable and biodegradable.
items.answer: Its monomer, lactic acid, is made by fermenting plant sugars (renewable); its ester links are hydrolysed and the products broken down by microorganisms (biodegradable).
items.markingKey: Its monomer, lactic acid, is made by fermenting plant sugars (renewable) [1]; its ester links are hydrolysed and the products broken down by microorganisms (biodegradable) [1] [2]

items.stem: Chloe says: "Biodegradable polymers are addition polymers like poly(ethene)." Explain whether Chloe is correct.
items.answer: Most biodegradable polymers are condensation polymers (polyesters, polyamides) with hydrolysable links.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Most biodegradable polymers are condensation polymers (polyesters, polyamides) with hydrolysable links. [2]

items.stem: Strips of a poly(butylene succinate) film were buried in compost at 40 °C and weighed every two weeks: week 0: 3.73 g, week 2: 3.42 g, week 4: 3.14 g, week 6: 2.88 g, week 8: 2.64 g. Calculate the percentage loss in mass over 8 weeks and the mean rate of mass loss in g per week.
items.answer: 29.2%; 0.136 g per week

items.stem: A city council in Colombo is choosing between bags made of poly(ethene), photodegradable poly(ethene) containing C=O groups, and PLA. (a) Explain how the photodegradable bag breaks down and why this may not work in landfill. (b) Explain how PLA biodegrades, naming the type of reaction involved.
items.answer: (a) C=O groups absorb UV, causing bond fission in the chain; buried bags receive no UV light. (b) Hydrolysis of the ester links (by water/enzymes) to lactic acid, which microorganisms convert to CO₂ and H₂O.
items.markingKey: (a) mechanism [1]; landfill limitation [1] [2] (b) hydrolysis of ester links [1]; products broken down [1] [2]

items.stem: Which linkage is present in proteins?
items.answer: –CONH– (peptide/amide)
items.markingKey: Proteins are polyamides.

items.stem: A student in Lima states: "The repeat unit of a polyester formed from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid contains one monomer." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: For an AA–BB polymer the repeat unit contains one residue of each monomer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: For an AA–BB polymer the repeat unit contains one residue of each monomer. [2]

items.stem: Tomás says: "Proteins are addition polymers of amino acids." Explain whether Tomás is correct.
items.answer: Proteins are condensation polymers: water is eliminated as each peptide bond forms.

items.stem: The condensation polymer nylon-6,6 is made from hexane-1,6-diamine (H₂N(CH₂)₆NH₂) and hexanedioyl dichloride (ClOC(CH₂)₄COCl). What type of polymer is it, and which small molecule is eliminated?

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "biodegradable polymer"?
options: A polymer that can be broken down by microorganisms in the environment into small molecules such as CO₂ and water.
A polymer that breaks down when it absorbs ultraviolet light, usually because it contains C=O groups.
Describes a polymer, such as poly(ethene), that is not broken down by microorganisms because it has no reactive polar groups.
The breaking of ester or amide links in a condensation polymer by reaction with water, catalysed by acid, alkali or enzymes.
items.answer: A polymer that can be broken down by microorganisms in the environment into small molecules such as CO₂ and water.
items.markingKey: Biodegradable polymer: a polymer that can be broken down by microorganisms in the environment into small molecules such as CO₂ and water.
